name: Can bathroom plumbing be relocated during a partial remodel instead of a full gut?

mainEntity.name: Can bathroom plumbing be relocated during a partial remodel instead of a full gut?
mainEntity.text: Can bathroom plumbing be relocated during a partial remodel instead of a full gut?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom plumbing can sometimes be relocated during a partial remodel, but the feasibility depends on access and how much finish material must be removed to reach the pipes. Smaller moves, such as a vanity shift, may fit well into a partial project if only one wall or section of flooring needs to be opened. Larger changes, especially toilet and shower relocations, often require more demolition because the drain, vent, and waterproofing systems are all affected. Once those systems are opened, the project can start to behave like a full gut remodel even if the original plan was partial. Homeowners should ask whether the plumbing route can be completed without damaging more finished surfaces than expected. If the answer involves slab cutting, subfloor repair, or extensive tile replacement, a full remodel may be the more efficient choice. The right decision comes down to access, budget, and how much of the bathroom is being reworked.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if the pipe route is accessible and the finish areas around it can be opened and repaired. Partial remodels work best for smaller relocations, while major toilet or shower moves often push the project toward a full gut.
